StatementEnd.Rule: Physical newlines inside parentheses and brackets never emit STATEMENT_END.
Newlines inside braces are context-sensitive: declaration/statement boundaries may emit STATEMENT_END; aggregate expression continuation does not.
A newline after a token requiring a right-hand operand does not emit STATEMENT_END.
StatementEnd.CanTerminate: IDENT INTEGER FLOAT STRING BYTE_STRING CHAR true false null undefined ) ] } return break continue

MlxLexicalSpecification.IntegerLiterals: decimal, 0x hexadecimal, 0b binary, 0o octal; underscore separators allowed between digits
MlxLexicalSpecification.FloatLiterals: decimal IEEE source syntax with optional exponent; source literal type is comptime_float

StringLiterals.Escapes: \n \r \t \0 \\ \" \' \xHH (one byte, two hexadecimal digits) \u{H..H} (a Unicode scalar, one to six hexadecimal digits, encoded as UTF-8)
StringLiterals.Rule: A backslash followed by anything else makes the literal invalid; the lexer reports it.
The length of a literal counts the bytes the escapes produce, not the source characters.

MlxLexicalSpecification.CharacterLiterals: Unicode scalar values only; the same escapes as string literals, \xHH standing for the scalar HH

Operators.Rule: When operator tokens share a prefix, the lexer emits the longest valid token.
Every valid shift-combine token also has a compound-assignment token formed by appending '='.
